decisions.name: Corollary 8.3 (vanishing of every indefinite integral implies the integrand is $0$ almost everywhere)
decisions.reason: This is Bass's one-dimensional indefinite-integral corollary. The measure-theoretic core is harvested here, but the interval-by-interval endpoint formulation belongs more naturally with the seam page comparing Lebesgue and Riemann integration, where indefinite integrals are already under discussion.
decisions.evidence: On Thursday, August 27, 2026, Bass still separates Proposition 8.2 from Corollary 8.3: the source harvest includes Proposition 8.2 under `thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality`, while Corollary 8.3 remains the one-dimensional interval/indefinite-integral specialization. The live MT-8 page on disk still closes at the general Lebesgue-integral and convergence-theorem spine, and `research/plan-spec.json` still places `the-lebesgue-and-riemann-integrals-compared` at order 288.017 immediately after MT-8. The deferment to that seam page therefore stands.

decisions.name: Theorem 1.19, measurable sets are G_delta or F_sigma modulo null sets
decisions.reason: This theorem is about the full completed Stieltjes-measure domain modulo null sets, while this page stops at the Borel correspondence, interval formulas, regularity, and the finite atomic decomposition.
decisions.evidence: The live MT-6 manifest already stops at the Borel correspondence, interval formulas, regularity on R, Cantor measure, and finite atomic-plus-atomless decomposition. Folland's Theorem 1.19 moves to completed-domain approximation of measurable sets modulo null sets, and no item on `lebesgue-stieltjes-measures-and-distribution-functions` or its companion cites or needs that stronger completion-level statement. This is therefore a real scope boundary inside the current page, not a hidden missing lemma.
